results.title: Heavy vs light flight on one rotation
results.rationale: T1 flies a light feeder cycle (DEL-JAI-DEL, 40 + 45 pax) before a full trunk cycle (DEL-BOM-DEL, 180 + 170 pax). Jaipur closes 06:30-09:30, so the feeder returns 2.5 h late and pushes the trunk flight into Mumbai's 13:00-17:00 curfew: waiting for the curfew to end would exceed the delay cap, so both trunk legs would be force-cancelled (350 pax). No spare aircraft exists: T3 is removed and T2 is already airborne on F5 (09:00) when the trunk flight needs an aircraft. Cancelling the light feeder cycle early keeps T1 at Delhi and protects the trunk rotation: 85 passengers lose their flight instead of 350. Cancelling only F1 would strand the aircraft at Delhi anyway but turn F2 into a forced cancellation, so the cycle is the clean decision.

The lowest impact decision removes the F3/F4 cycle explicitly (its passengers re-accommodate onto the delayed F5/F6) rather than letting the cascade decide. Swapping aircraft changes nothing: the constraint is the runway.

results.title: CAT-III qualification is the binding constraint
results.rationale: Delhi goes into low-visibility procedures 08:30-12:30. Crew C2 (F3/F4) is not CAT-III qualified, crews C1 and C3 are. The engine must recognise that the constraint is qualification, not duty time: the CAT-III standby S1 takes F3 and F4, nothing is cancelled, and F3 departs on time inside the fog. Doing nothing is the right decision - the standby call-out happens inside the propagation.

results.title: Crew-shortage day - several crews time out at once
results.rationale: Three rostered crews at Delhi become unavailable at 04:10 and only one standby exists. F1/F2 (C1), F3/F4 (C2) and F5/F6 (C3) all need crews; at most one cycle can be saved. The standby goes to the cycle that carries the most passengers and connections (F3/F4). The standby would otherwise be consumed by the first departure (F1), so F1/F2 must be cancelled explicitly to free it, and the F5/F6 cycle cancelled early and explicitly so their passengers are re-accommodated onto whatever still flies. The naive rule cancels by passenger count and leaves the rest to be forced at the gate.
